from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence", 
                          ["A series is the limit of partial sums.", 
                           "Standard distance shrinks towards zero.", 
                           "Geometric series converge on a number line."])
        
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualizing a sequence approaching a limit
        number_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 2, 0.5], length=4, include_numbers=True)
        self.place_in_area(number_line, 'C1', 'C6')
        
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(number_line.n2p(0))
        
        self.play(Create(number_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        # Move dot to 1 (partial sums 0.5, 0.75, 0.875, 0.9375...)
        partial_sums = [0.5, 0.75, 0.875, 0.9375, 1.0]
        for val in partial_sums:
            self.play(dot.animate.move_to(number_line.n2p(val)), run_time=0.5)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight distance shrinking
        dist_brace = Brace(Line(start=number_line.n2p(0.9375), end=number_line.n2p(1)), UP)
        dist_label = Text("d(s_n, s)", font_size=18).next_to(dist_brace, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(dist_brace), Write(dist_label))
        self.play(FadeOut(dist_brace), FadeOut(dist_label))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Showing the geometric series segment
        rect = Rectangle(width=4, height=0.2, color=YELLOW_D, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(rect, 'E1', 'E6')
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introducing the 2-adic Metric", [
            "Shift perspective to the 2-adic norm.",
            "Divisibility by 2 defines 'smallness'.",
            "High powers of 2 are very small."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        math_formula = MathTex("|x|_2 = 2^{-v_2(x)}", font_size=48)
        exponent_part = math_formula.get_part_by_tex("-v_2(x)")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(math_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(math_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(exponent_part, color=BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Represent smallness with scaling
        power_2 = MathTex("2^3 = 8", font_size=40, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(power_2, 'E2')
        self.play(FadeIn(power_2))
        self.play(power_2.animate.scale(0.3).move_to(self.grid['E5']))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Infinite Sums in 2-adic Space", [
            "Convergence means terms approach zero.", 
            "Terms become increasingly divisible by 2.", 
            "The sum 1+2+4+8 converges to -1."
        ])

        # Reveal lecture lines sequentially
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a series of 2-adic terms (approaching 0)
        terms = VGroup(*[MathTex(f"2^{{{i}}}") for i in range(5)])
        for i, term in enumerate(terms):
            self.place_at_grid(term, f"B{i+1}", scale_factor=0.8)
            self.play(Write(term))
        
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture[0]), FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate terms shifting left/becoming more divisible
        self.play(*[Indicate(term, color=BLUE) for term in terms])
        
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture[1]), FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show partial sum 1+2+4+8 = 15 = -1 mod 16
        sum_text = MathTex("1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \\dots = -1")
        self.place_at_grid(sum_text, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(sum_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The ultrametric inequality forbids standard stretching.", "|x+y| is at most max(|x|, |y|).", "Distances do not add up normally."]
        self.setup_layout("The Ultrametric Inequality", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        disk1 = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        disk2 = Circle(radius=0.75, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3)
        label1 = MathTex(r"|x|_2 = 2^{-1}").set_color(BLUE)
        label2 = MathTex(r"|y|_2 = 2^{-2}").set_color(GREEN)
        formula = MathTex(r"|x+y|_2 \leq \max(|x|_2, |y|_2)").scale(1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "C4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(disk1), Write(label1.next_to(disk1, UP)))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "C5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(disk2), Write(label2.next_to(disk2, DOWN)))
        self.play(FadeIn(formula.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.0)))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Highlight disjointness/containment
        self.play(
            Indicate(disk1),
            Indicate(disk2),
            formula.animate.set_color(ORANGE)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application and Summary", [
            "2-adic distance solves number theory problems.",
            "Infinity behaves differently in 2-adic space.",
            "Infinite series can be contained integers."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 2-adic distance solves number theory problems.
        concept = Text("2-adic Logic", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(concept, "B2")
        self.play(Write(concept))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Infinity behaves differently in 2-adic space.
        infinity_sign = MathTex(r"\infty", color=BLUE).scale(2)
        label = Text("Infinite?", color=BLUE, font_size=20)
        group = VGroup(infinity_sign, label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(group, "D4")
        self.play(FadeIn(group))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Infinite series can be contained integers.
        series = MathTex(r"1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \dots = -1", color=GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(series, "E1", "F6")
        self.play(Write(series))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence
sections.content: Briefly define a series as the limit of partial sums. Introduce the standard Euclidean metric (distance) where a series converges if its terms get smaller and approach zero.
sections.example: Visualizing the Geometric Series 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... as a shrinking segment on a standard number line, clearly converging to 1.

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
sections.content: Shift the perspective. Define the 2-adic norm |x|_2: a number is 'small' if it is divisible by a high power of 2. Contrast this with Euclidean space.
sections.example: A 'Number Magnifying Glass' animation: In 2-adic space, 8 (2^3) is very small (distance 1/8 to 0), whereas 1/8 is very large (distance 8 to 0). Everything is inverted.

sections.title: Infinite Sums in 2-adic Space
sections.content: Explain the surprising convergence rule: A series converges in the 2-adic metric if and only if the terms approach zero in the 2-adic sense (i.e., they are increasingly divisible by 2).
sections.example: Consider the series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... + 2^n. In Euclidean space, this explodes to infinity. In 2-adic space, this is a Cauchy sequence that converges to -1.

sections.title: The Ultrametric Inequality (The 'No-Overlap' Rule)
sections.content: Introduce the strong triangle inequality: |x + y|_2 ≤ max(|x|_2, |y|_2). This eliminates the 'stretching' effect of standard addition.
sections.example: A visual demonstration using a fractal tree (Sierpinski-like): paths never overlap in ways that 'add up' normally; they essentially choose the largest 'branch' or power of 2.

sections.title: Application and Summary
sections.content: Summarize how changing the definition of distance allows us to solve number theory problems. Wrap up with the idea that infinity is not a fixed concept.
sections.example: A character, 'Detective 2-adic', uses the 2-adic lens to solve a riddle: showing that something appearing 'infinite' in our normal world is actually a neatly contained integer in the 2-adic world.
